title: Hirmenschelis: John's testament family
standfirst: John's 1577 estate administration identifies his widow and two children. His place in the burgh pedigree remains open. The Huchesoun strip supplied with the testament has an unresolved date, archival reference and family connection.
question: Was the Hirmenschelis testator the John in the burgh protocols, and can the Huchesoun fragment help identify Margaret?
answer: The testament records Margaret as John's widow and identifies Katherine and Marjory as his lawful children and executors-dative. Their inheritance shares, Margaret's surname and the children's maternity remain unresolved. The burgh identity and the fragment's connection to the family remain open.

chapters.title: A small family at administration
body: The Edinburgh Commissary Court index records the testament on 4 May 1577 and describes John as being in Hirmenschelis. The testament says he died in March. The year is unresolved, and the registration supplies only an upper bound.

Margaret submitted the inventory on behalf of Katherine and Marjory, John's lawful children and court-appointed executors-dative. That appointment establishes their administrative role. Their inheritance shares remain unresolved. The widow could be the woman represented by [Margaret Hutcheson](/people/hutcheson-1656.html). Her surname remains unresolved. The unclear possessive in the lawful-children clause leaves their maternity unresolved.

chapters.title: The undated Huchesoun strip
body: Strip 396A was supplied with images of John’s testament. Its heading identifies Andro Huchesoun’s confirmation. The body includes the word bairnis (children) and a provisional reading of Johne Huchesoun.
The strip’s own archival reference and date are unresolved. The wording read so far leaves the children’s parentage and any connection with John or Margaret open.
